implementation: The library and business main retain crate/module forbid(unsafe_code); no business unsafe call/definition or scoped unsafe lint override remains.

Platform entry and standalone adapters register three fixed typed capabilities once. Pure-data HelperStartup/LookupInput fields remain opaque; safe spawn accepts the audited capability, not an arbitrary function.

Each fork checks a fresh ProcessOwner critical section; live threads and panic-handler reentry fail before fork. Runtime checks prove thread conditions only; adapter registration documents the separate callback, allocator/NSS, mapping and inherited-resource obligations.

Fork workers forget inherited panic-hook captures and install a silent hook before abandoning descriptors. The successful detached service retains its original hook; only terminating startup branches replace it.

Packaging copies the new platform entry/registration/test files. The platform subcrate disables automatic discovery of parent-package adapters; its existing library unit tests remain enabled. Three lockfiles only add path dependency relationships; all registry package blocks are unchanged.
new_negative_controls: Before registration, helper and resolver starts return explicit missing-worker errors.

After registration, a live std thread makes both starts fail without changing SigBlk, descriptor numbers or child list; after join, only transient EINVAL is retried at the real resolver boundary, and resolver/helper then complete.

A child panic neither invokes nor drops an inherited custom hook capture and exits 5. The parent hook remains installed, and attempting Helper::start from that hook returns the explicit panic-handler rejection.
performance_scope: No DNS/DHCP packet-processing hot path changed. New process checks run only at fork boundaries; this task ran correctness gates and no CPU benchmark.
